segments.text: Octopuses have one heart. Well, that's not exactly true. They have three.
Two of them pump blood through the gills. The third one pumps it to the rest of the body.
Here's the wild part. When an octopus swims, that third heart stops beating. Which is why they'd rather crawl. Swimming literally wears them out.
And their blood? It's blue. Instead of iron, it uses copper to carry oxygen, which works better in cold, deep water.
That's not all. An octopus has about {500 million|five hundred million} neurons, and two thirds of them aren't in its head. They're in its arms.
Each arm can taste what it touches, and even make some decisions on its own.
In fact, they can change color in a split second, even though they're probably colorblind.
And there are no bones. If its beak fits through a hole, the whole octopus fits through.
So next time someone says octopuses have one heart, tell them it's three. And one of them hates swimming.
